items.title: Inventory spec flags, mmproj compatibility and the recorded traffic
items.instructions: Write bench/m1_recon.py and submit it as a `run` request (no GPU needed). It must write everything into bench/results/<run date>/m1-ngram/recon/: (a) help.txt = full output of `~/Projects/llama.cpp-bonsai2/build/bin/llama-server --help`, plus spec_flags.txt containing only the lines for --spec-type, --spec-ngram-*, --draft-* and --spec-*. (b) spec_mmproj_grep.txt = every line (with file:line) under ~/Projects/llama.cpp-bonsai2/tools/server/ that matches 'speculative' or 'spec' within 5 lines of 'mtmd', 'multimodal' or 'mctx'. This tells us whether the server refuses or disables speculation when --mmproj is loaded. (c) inventory.json for /home/josiah/Projects/bonsai-garden/evals/results/2026-10-11-baseline-mem0/: for each run dir and step, the events file path and size, the number of assistant messages, the number of tool calls by tool name, and the event `type` values that occur with counts. Also include the run's tap.jsonl records for that step (role, n_messages, timings.prompt_n, timings.cache_n, timings.predicted_n), and whether mem0 SQLite files (*.db) exist and which tables and row counts they have. (d) event_samples.json = one full, untruncated example of each distinct event type from one mem0-arm step, so the schema is visible in the sandbox. (e) sources.txt = the paths of the installed pi package and of mem0ai's dist/oss/index.mjs (search evals/.cache and the run dirs). From mem0, extract the full ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT constant and the source of the function that builds the extraction user prompt into mem0_extract_src.txt. From pi's dist, extract the function that builds the system prompt and the built-in tool JSON schemas into pi_prompt_src.txt. After the run, write bench/m1-notes.md: which spec types and tuning flags exist, with their defaults; whether spec + mmproj looks supported (quote the lines); the event schema (how to rebuild an OpenAI messages list from it); and how mem0's user prompt is assembled. Commit the script, the recon outputs and the notes.
items.acceptance: bench/results/*/m1-ngram/recon/ contains help.txt, spec_flags.txt, spec_mmproj_grep.txt, inventory.json, event_samples.json, sources.txt, mem0_extract_src.txt and pi_prompt_src.txt, all non-empty. inventory.json covers every step*.events.jsonl in the source dir and includes tap prompt_n/cache_n per request. bench/m1-notes.md lists the available --spec-type values and the ngram/draft flags with their defaults, states an explicit yes/no/unclear for spec+mmproj with quoted source lines, and describes the message-rebuild mapping. Committed on auto/M1-ngram.

items.title: Convert recordings into agent and mem0 replay requests, checked against tap prompt sizes
items.instructions: Write bench/build_replay_set.py and run it via a `run` request. Output goes to bench/.replay/m1/ (add bench/.replay/ to .gitignore; recorded content stays out of git). (1) agent.jsonl: one line per recorded agent LLM request, i.e. each assistant turn. Fields: id ('<run>/<step>/<turn>'), body (OpenAI /v1/chat/completions body: messages = system prompt + full history before that turn, assistant reasoning dropped as pi does, tool_calls and tool results kept; tools = pi's tool schemas, plus mem0_memory in the mem0 arm), recorded_prompt_tokens (prompt_n+cache_n of the matching tap.jsonl record, matched by run, step, role=agent and order). Rebuild the system prompt from pi_prompt_src.txt. If that isn't possible, use a stand-in of the same length in characters, and set system_prompt_exact=false in the manifest. Choose turns from at least 4 different steps across both arms, up to 30 requests total, and prefer steps with file reads, edits and test output. (2) mem.jsonl: one line per rebuilt mem0 extraction call, up to 12, built from the mem0-arm runs. System = ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT verbatim. User prompt is assembled as in mem0_extract_src.txt: the existing memories come from that run's SQLite store, filtered to entries created before the call where timestamps allow; the recent and new messages are the user prompt plus the first assistant text, taken from the events. Add chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking:false}, plus recorded_prompt_tokens from the matching tap role=mem record. Do not put sampling params in the bodies; the probe sets them. (3) Commit bench/results/<run date>/m1-ngram/replay_manifest.json. Per request it holds id, role, n_messages, prompt chars, chars/4 estimate, recorded_prompt_tokens and est/recorded ratio. It also holds totals and system_prompt_exact.
items.acceptance: .gitignore contains bench/.replay/. replay_manifest.json is committed and lists 20–30 agent requests from ≥4 distinct steps and 6–12 mem requests (or a documented reason mem is infeasible). Every entry has recorded_prompt_tokens. The median est/recorded ratio is within 0.75–1.33 for each role, and outliers are explained in bench/m1-notes.md. The builder script is committed and runnable as `python3 bench/build_replay_set.py`.

items.title: Replay probe on :8089: spec off vs ≥2 n-gram settings, 1 and 2 slots busy
items.instructions: Write bench/spec_replay.py OUTDIR LABEL SAMPLING [extra server args...], with SAMPLING one of greedy|prod. Server: take the cmd block of serving/llama-swap.bonsai-2-27b.yaml verbatim, replace ${PORT} with 8089, set LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1 and append the extra args, so the flags exactly match production (-np 2, --kv-unified, --mmproj, q4_0 KV). If the server exits or logs that speculation is disabled because of mmproj, record that in OUTDIR/LABEL/notes.txt, then rerun that config with --mmproj/--no-mmproj-offload removed, labelled '<LABEL>-nommproj' (and the off config likewise for a fair baseline). Phases, each on a FRESH server start, because the n-gram pool persists across requests and replaying identical requests would inflate acceptance: single-agent (agent.jsonl in order on id_slot 0, slot 1 idle); single-mem (mem.jsonl on id_slot 1); dual-agent (agent.jsonl foreground on slot 0, while a background thread loops mem.jsonl on slot 1 until the foreground finishes); dual-mem (mem foreground on slot 1, agent loop in background on slot 0). Sampling: greedy = temperature 0, top_k 1, seed 0 for both roles; prod = agent temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, seed 0, and mem temperature 0.2, seed 0. Use max_tokens 768 for agent and 1024 for mem, non-streaming. Write OUTDIR/LABEL-SAMPLING/requests.jsonl (committed) with one line per request: phase, role, fg|bg, id, slot, prompt_n, cache_n, predicted_n, predicted_ms, predicted_per_second, draft_n, draft_n_accepted, finish_reason, tool_call_json_valid (bool), out_sha256 over reasoning_content+content+tool_calls. Full output texts go to bench/.replay/m1/outputs/LABEL-SAMPLING.jsonl (gitignored). Also record vram.txt (nvidia-smi after the first request of each phase) and keep the server logs. Submit one `run` request per (config, sampling) under a turnstile lease, in this order: off/greedy; A/greedy where A = `--spec-type ngram-mod` with defaults; B/greedy where B is a second setting chosen from spec_flags.txt (another ngram type, or ngram-mod with a different draft size), with the choice justified in bench/m1-notes.md; then prod sampling for off and for whichever of A/B had the higher dual-agent greedy decode tok/s.
items.acceptance: bench/spec_replay.py is committed. bench/results/*/m1-ngram/ has requests.jsonl, vram.txt and server logs for off-greedy, A-greedy, B-greedy, off-prod and best-prod, each with all 4 phases present. Every foreground request in the A/B runs has draft_n and draft_n_accepted fields. For any config where draft_n is 0 across all requests, notes.txt explains why (e.g. mmproj refusal), with the server log line quoted. The mmproj outcome is stated in bench/m1-notes.md.

items.title: Summarize, decide, and deploy via infra only if the rule is met
items.instructions: Write bench/spec_summarize.py, which reads the requests.jsonl files and the gitignored outputs and writes bench/results/<date>/m1-ngram/summary.md and summary.json. Use foreground requests only. Table per (config, sampling, phase, role): n, token-weighted decode tok/s = sum(predicted_n)/sum(predicted_ms)*1000, median per-request tok/s, acceptance = sum(draft_n_accepted)/sum(draft_n), draft tokens per generated token, speedup vs off at the same sampling and phase, tool_call_json_valid rate, and VRAM vs off. Identity table (greedy only): for each spec config and phase, the count of requests whose out_sha256 equals off's for the same phase and id, and for mismatches the first-divergence character index. Include the control off/dual vs off/single, so batch-numerics divergence is visible. Decision rule, written into summary.md: deploy the best config only if (1) it runs with --mmproj loaded (the live entry's pinned line); (2) at prod sampling, dual-agent tok/s ≥ 1.10× off; (3) dual-mem and both single phases ≥ 0.97× off; (4) VRAM ≤ off + 64 MiB; (5) tool_call_json_valid rate ≥ off's; (6) greedy identical-output rate is not below the off dual-vs-single control by more than 10 points. If deploying: create serving/candidates/bonsai-2-27b.ngram.yaml, a copy of serving/llama-swap.bonsai-2-27b.yaml with only the spec flags added to cmd and a header comment citing summary.md, and submit an `infra` request. Save the returned JSON as bench/results/<date>/m1-ngram/deploy.json. On 'applied', update serving/llama-swap.bonsai-2-27b.yaml to match, with an APPLIED header like the existing one. If not deploying, write deploy.json as {"deployed": false, "why": [failed rule numbers with values]} and make no infra request.
items.acceptance: summary.md and summary.json are committed, contain all the tables above with numbers that recompute from requests.jsonl, and state each of the 6 rules as pass/fail with values. deploy.json exists. If deployed, it holds infra.py's result with result='applied', single_tok_s and conc_tok_s, and serving/llama-swap.bonsai-2-27b.yaml differs from the previous version only in the spec flags and the header. If not deployed, no file exists under serving/candidates/ and the live-entry yaml is unchanged.

items.title: Experiment page, series and project summaries, docs
items.instructions: Follow site/AUTHORING.md. Create site/series/serving/ngram-speculation.md (layer: experiment, series: serving, status: done, date = probe date, updated = today, tldr, summary ≤200 words). The summary covers the question, the method (replayed recorded pi turns and rebuilt mem0 calls, fresh server per phase, greedy and prod sampling), the headline numbers (dual-agent and dual-mem tok/s off vs best, acceptance), the mmproj finding and the decision. The body holds the summary tables copied from summary.md, the identity/control result, the caveats (a stand-in system prompt if one was used, approximate mem0 user prompts, max_tokens caps, the outputs diverging from the recordings), and links to the scripts and results on GitHub as the other pages do. If deployed, include deploy.json's health numbers and note that the 3-session soak is in progress or done. Update site/series/serving/index.md: revise the summary and the 'Deferred ideas' n-gram bullet, and bump updated. Update site/index.md: summary and 'So far'/'Next', a Trajectory entry, bump updated. Update docs/engine-review.md §3 item 2 and the Phase C line with the result; docs/roadmap.md M1 row/status line; and README.md next steps. Run `python3 tools/check_site.py`.
items.acceptance: site/series/serving/ngram-speculation.md exists with valid front matter and a summary of ≤200 words. Every number in it matches summary.md or deploy.json. The series index and site/index.md have updated ≥ the experiment's updated, and their summaries mention the M1 outcome. docs/engine-review.md, docs/roadmap.md and README.md reflect the result. `python3 tools/check_site.py` passes, with its output pasted into the final journal entry.
